What we do

Most jobs start as a leak or a damaged patch. We fix what is wrong, and tell you plainly if a full replacement is the better choice.

Roof leak repair

We trace the leak to its source, repair or replace the damaged section, and test it. No guessing, no covering a problem with sealant.

Metal sheet roofing

New or replacement GI, aluminium and coated sheet roofs for houses, sheds, workshops and shops, fixed with proper screws and sealing washers.

Tile roofing

Re-laying, replacing broken or slipped tiles, ridge and valley repair, and reinforcing the frame underneath.

Trusses and framework

Metal and wood trusses for new roofs and extensions, and strengthening of weak or sagging structures.

Waterproofing

Terrace and flat-roof waterproofing, crack sealing, and damp prevention before the monsoon starts.

Gutters and sheet fitting

Gutters, downpipes, flashing and skylight sheets so water leaves the roof the way it should.

Recent work

Roofs, metal frameworks and staircases from our own jobs.

Gates, handrails and staircases

We also make and fit gates, handrails and staircases, built to suit your house: sliding and swing gates, balcony and staircase handrails, and staircases for terraces and rooftops.

Common questions

How do I know if I need a repair or a new roof?

We check the sheets or tiles, the fixings and the frame during the inspection. If a repair will hold, we say so. If the structure is worn out, we explain why and what replacement involves.

Is the inspection really free?

Yes. We look at the roof, take photos and give you a written quote. You decide whether to go ahead.

How long will the work take?

It depends on the size of the roof and the type of work. The written quote includes an estimated timeline.

Can you fix a leak during the rains?

We can usually patch an active leak to stop damage. Larger repairs and new roofing are best done in dry weather, so we plan them with you.

How do I get a quote?

Fill in the form below or call us. We will agree a time to visit and give you the quote in writing.
